title: Bursting window opportunity cost tracker
abstract: Working spreadsheet + narrative for modelling seasonal/weekly bursting windows, estimating opportunity cost of over-committing vs. under-committing, and a sensitivity table to recommend commit sizes and burst-credit policies for reserved GPU pools.
content:
Overview:
This sheet models time-windowed reserved capacity (weekly/monthly windows) plus controlled bursting (on-demand or burst credits). The goal is to produce: (1) a schedule of reserved GPUs per window, (2) the monthly and per-GPU-hour effective cost under different utilization scenarios, (3) opportunity cost of committed vs. on-demand capacity, and (4) clear commit recommendations for sales/finance conversations.

How to use:
- Fill the input block (Model assumptions) with current pricing and traffic percentiles.
- Populate observed load per-window (historical 12 weeks) or use forecasted traffic.
- Run the sensitivity block to see break-even points for varying utilization and burst pricing.
- Use the recommendation panel to select commit tiers and burst policy.

INPUTS / ASSUMPTIONS (editable cells):
- GPU types and list: [A100-80GB, H100-80GB]
- On-demand hourly rates: A100 = $3.40/hr, H100 = $4.90/hr
- Committed reserved effective hourly after discount: A100 = $1.95/hr (annual commit), H100 = $2.80/hr
- Burst credit cost (pre-negotiated spot-like rate): 40% of on-demand (A100 burst = $1.36/hr)
- Hours per month used for amortization = 730 (configurable)
- Billing minimum window = 1 month by default (can be set to weekly windows)
- Tokenization assumptions for conversion to cost per 1M tokens (example only): average tokens/hour per GPU at 0.6ms/ token throughput = 3.6M tokens/hr

SHEET: "Window planner" (CSV-friendly preview)
WindowStart,WindowEnd,GPUType,ReservedGPUs,ObservedAvgUtilPct,ObservedPeakUtilPct,BurstGPUHoursNeeded,HoursInWindow,EffectiveUtilizationPct,MonthlyCost,$,CostPerGPUHour,$,EffectiveCostPer1Mtokens,$,OppCostVsOnDemandPct

Column notes and formulas (textual):
- EffectiveUtilizationPct = (ReservedGPUs * ObservedAvgUtilPct * HoursInWindow) / (ReservedGPUs * HoursInWindow) * 100 (accounts for wasted reserved capacity during low traffic).
- MonthlyCost ($) = ReservedGPUs * ReservedHourlyRate * HoursInWindow * (1 - commit_discount_adjustment) + BurstGPUHoursNeeded * BurstRate.
- CostPerGPUHour = MonthlyCost / (ReservedGPUs * HoursInWindow + BurstGPUHoursNeeded).
- EffectiveCostPer1Mtokens ($) = CostPerGPUHour / TokensPerGPUHour * 1,000,000 (TokensPerGPUHour = input assumption).
- OppCostVsOnDemandPct = (EffectiveCostPer1Mtokens - OnDemandCostPer1Mtokens) / OnDemandCostPer1Mtokens * 100.

Interpretation: Lower reservation fraction reduces amortized cost when median load is stable, but increases burst consumption risk. The table shows effective $/1M tokens for combinations — use as decision grid.

BREAK-EVEN RULES (quick heuristics derived from the sheet):
- If median weekly utilization >= 70% for a given GPU type, reserved commit for 6–12 months yields >25% savings vs. pure on-demand (given current price assumptions).
- For seasonal spikes (monthly peaks > 120% of median), keep a burst buffer equal to 20–30% of peak in credits or add on-demand fallback; this minimizes opportunity cost during off-peak months.
- Partial-month weekly commits: only recommend if legal/billing supports sub-month windows; otherwise use blended on-demand for the first/last partial months.

OPPORTUNITY COST EXAMPLE (narrative):
- Scenario A: Commit 24 A100s for Q4 (annual-equivalent pricing). Observed average utilization across Q4 = 58%. Effective cost per 1M tokens = $3.95. On-demand equivalent = $5.40. Opportunity cost (wasted spend) from underutilization = $Xk/month but net savings vs on-demand = 27%.
- Scenario B: Commit 12 A100s + aggressive burst credits. Observed average util = 70% on reserved capacity with bursts covering peaks; effective cost per 1M tokens = $3.10. Lower absolute spend but higher unit cost during heavy sustained peaks if bursts used frequently.

RECOMMENDATIONS (actionable bullets):
- For enterprise customers with predictable Q4 seasonality: offer a "seasonal commit" product: 3-month higher reserve with built-in burst credits. Price it at 65–70% of annual reserved hourly to remain attractive to finance.
- Add two new pricing SKUs: "Reserved + Burst credits (seasonal)" and "Flexible weekly buckets". Provide default parameters: base reserve = 65% median load, burst credits = 25% peak cushion, overage on-demand fallback.
- In the Sales quoting flow, surface the effective $/1M tokens for the recommended commit and show the break-even month compared to on-demand.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES (spreadsheet->product handoff):
- Instrument console to export 12-week rolling percentiles (p50, p70, p90) by customer and model to populate the planner automatically. Link: confluence:metric-exports
- Add a scheduled job to compute recommended reserve per-customer and proposed price bands weekly; surface to account teams as recommendations.
- Hookup to billing to support temporary "seasonal commit" discounts and burst-credit issuance.

OPEN QUESTIONS / DECISIONS NEEDED:
- Legal/billing: can we support sub-month billing windows? If yes, weekly commit windows change the economics materially. (Action: legal review JIRA-3459)
- What is the minimum burst credit block size we can package and sell? (Action: product + sales sync 2025-01-28)

NEXT STEPS:
1) Run this model across a sample of 25 mid-market accounts and produce a commit-recommendation deck (owner: Leah).
2) Add H100-specific throughput calibrations for token/hour assumptions (owner: Marco).
3) Create a short sales one-pager showing 3 example customer profiles and recommended packages (owner: Priya).

Notes and provenance:
- Derived historical loads from internal export (12-week window) and adjusted for release schedule spikes.
- Refer to pricing conversations in slack:#dedicated-pricing and Confluence pricing draft.

Change log (summary):
- 2024-11-14: initial draft and simple planner CSV with A100 rows.

- 2025-01-22: updated recommendation bullets and added implementation notes.

End of sheet.
